chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Hashimi, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The woman who gives khul' (mutual divorce), the woman who gives mubarat (unilateral divorce by wife), and the woman who asks for istibra' (waiting period) in her divorce from her husband, inherit nothing if that was from them during the husband's illness, and even if he dies during his illness, because the bond of marriage has been severed from them and from him.'

key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِعَةُ: The woman who initiates khul' (divorce by redemption)
key_terms.وَالْمُبَارِئَةُ: The woman who initiates mubarat (unilateral divorce)
key_terms.وَالْمُسْتَأْمَرَةُ: The woman who seeks istibra' (waiting period)

ai.seo_question: Does a wife inherit from her husband if they divorce during his illness?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that in cases of *khul'* (wife-initiated divorce), *mubarat* (mutual divorce), or *istibra'* (divorce by agreement), the wife forfeits her inheritance share if the husband dies during the 'illness of death' (*marad al-mawt*) because the marital bond (*'ismah*) is deemed severed by the agreement. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that these specific forms of divorce act as a complete dissolution of the marital tie for inheritance purposes, distinct from standard *talaq*. The principle underscores that the financial rights attached to the marriage contract are contingent upon the continuity of the bond at the time of death.
